newsitem.title: UK: Guinness says stout sales up over summer.
newsitem.headline: Guinness says stout sales up over summer.

text.p: Sales of draught Guinness were higher this summer than last year as the cooler weather attracted more drinkers to Guinness, said Jonathan Miller, communications manager at Guinness Brewing Worldwide.

"Guinness sales this summer were well up on last year. It's simply because it wasn't as hot this year so stout sales were higher. Last year it was so hot people started drinking lager and cider," said Miller.
Guinness is typically poured at eight degrees centigrade. In the sweltering summer of 1995 its sales were hit, amongst other things, by Caffrey's, a Bass cream ale served chilled.
"In the UK draught Guinness achieved its highest ever market share, breaking through the five percent barrier this summer and that was really helped by the new ad campaign," said Miller.
Guinness launched a televsion and poster campaign before the summer building on its "Black and White" theme. -- Tim Farrand, London Newsroom +44 71 542 6437
